item.title: N.D. Wilson
item.description: “The point is simply that the problem of evil leaves logic at home and goes out alone without a chaperone. The existence of evil in Hamlet in no way implies that Shakespeare lacked control in his heart, or that he was evil. The implication that Shakespeare didn’t exist is even more outlandish.” (Notes from the Tilt-a-Whirl, p. 98) She looked at me and leaned forward, waiting for the Protestant version. ‘“I don’t know,” I said.
item.content:
“The point is simply that the problem of evil leaves logic at home and goes out alone without a chaperone. The existence of evil in Hamlet in no way implies that Shakespeare lacked control in his heart, or that he was evil. The implication that Shakespeare didn’t exist is even more outlandish.” (Notes from the Tilt-a-Whirl, p. 98)

She looked at me and leaned forward, waiting for the Protestant version. ‘“I don’t know,” I said. “Don’t you want to?"’ ‘“What do you mean?” she made an excellent questioning face—cocked head and eyebrows behind glasses.’ “‘Why would I want to go to Hell?’ ‘God is who He is. Do you want to be with Him?’ Hell is voluntary. Would you like to go?” (Notes from the Tilt-a-Whirl, p. 175)

item.title: Unkown
item.description: “Another source of depression is distrustfulness. Let us rejoice in the present, and let us trust for the future. Let us pray and strive till our frame of mind is more in unison with the Lord’s kindness; and in every gracious providence and in every spiritual mercy bestowed on ourselves or others dear to us let us recognize the merciful kindness of the Lord, and let us acknowledge what we recognize.
item.content:
“Another source of depression is distrustfulness. Let us rejoice in the present, and let us trust for the future. Let us pray and strive till our frame of mind is more in unison with the Lord’s kindness; and in every gracious providence and in every spiritual mercy bestowed on ourselves or others dear to us let us recognize the merciful kindness of the Lord, and let us acknowledge what we recognize.” (“Speaking on Ecclesiastes 3:12–13”)

“It was for us that He was sorrowful even unto death; for us that He was heavy, for us that He was troubled. It was not the punishment of His own sins that weighed Him down, for He was sinless, but the punishment of ours. Love, and not His own guilt, made Him a partner in our misery.”

“God is better at forgiving than you are at sinning.” -Random guy from Twitter

item.content:
“The beauty which flows through men’s minds into their skillful hands comes from that Beauty which is above their souls and for which my soul sighs all day and night.” (Confessions 10.34) -Saint Augustine

“If it is inevitable it must be handeled immediately” -Athletic Director of Vanderbilt (2024)

“The decree of election does not require a decree of damnation. Whereas God has positively decreed the salvation of some, He permissively leaves the non-elect to their self-chosen rebellion and its natural consequence of punishment. ‘We should not see predestination as a grim process whereby God condemns great numbers of people to eternal loss. Rather, it is the outworking of a loving purpose whereby he delivers great numbers of people for salvation.’” -Constable’s Notes

“Holy Scripture can never lie or err, nevertheless some of its interpreters and expositors can sometimes err… [if they] limit themselves always to the literal meaning of the words…” -Galileo Galilei

“If you have to swallow two goldfish, swallow the biggest one first.”-Governor Ned Ray McWherter

“If God gives you an abundant harvest of trials, it is a sign of great holiness which He desires you to attain. Do you want to become a great saint? Ask God to send you many sufferings. The flame of Divine Love never rises higher than when fed with the wood of the Cross, which the infinite charity of the Savior used to finish His sacrifice. All the pleasures of the world are nothing compared with the sweetness found in the gall and vinegar offered to Jesus Christ. That is, hard and painful things endured for Jesus Christ and with Jesus Christ.” -Ignatius of Loyola

“Even faith is a gift of God. Intellectually harmonizing the sovereignty of God and the responsibility of people is impossible humanly, but perfectly resolved in the infinite mind of God.” (Note on John 6:40) -John MacArthur

“Jesus loves you is a true statement but it means nothing to the person that doesn’t understand that he shouldn’t be loved because he is an enemy of God. God should not love us.” -Keith Foskey

“We will not live our days wondering if we could have saved more.” (X-Men ‘97) -Magneto

“Ah, souls, you can easily sin as the saints—but can you repent with the saints? Many can sin with David and Peter, that cannot repent with David and Peter—and so must perish forever!” -Thomas Brooks

“Do you realize that it is only in the Gospel of Jesus Christ that you get the verdict before the performance?… In Christianity, the verdict leads to performance.” (The Freedom of Self-Forgetfulness, p. 39) -Timothy Keller

“If you take Christ out of Christian all you’re left with is Ian. Ian’s a great guy but he’s not going to save you from your sins.” (Joe Rogan #2252) -Wesley Huff

item.title: C.S. Lewis
item.description: “Perhaps we feel inclined to disagree with Him. But there is a difficulty about disagreeing with God. He is the source from which all your reasoning power comes: you could not be right and He wrong any more than a stream can rise higher than its own source. When you are arguing against Him you are arguing against the very power that makes you able to argue at all: it is like cutting off the branch you are sitting on.
item.content:
“Perhaps we feel inclined to disagree with Him. But there is a difficulty about disagreeing with God. He is the source from which all your reasoning power comes: you could not be right and He wrong any more than a stream can rise higher than its own source. When you are arguing against Him you are arguing against the very power that makes you able to argue at all: it is like cutting off the branch you are sitting on.” (Mere Christianity)

“Other vices may sometimes bring people together… but Pride always means enmity — it is enmity.” (Mere Christianity, p. 124)

“…the devil loves ‘curing’ a small fault by giving you a great one. We must try not to be vain, but we must never call in our Pride to cure our vanity.” (Mere Christianity, p. 127)

“There have been men before now who got so interested in proving the existence of God that they came to care nothing for God Himself … as if the good Lord had nothing to do but exist!” (The Great Divorce, p. 74)

item.title: Charles Spurgeon
item.description: “How frequently does the wearied pilgrim put up the prayer, ‘O that I had wings like a dove, for then would I fly away and be at rest.’ But Christ does not pray like that; he leaves it to his Father, until, like shocks of corn fully ripe, we shall each of us be gathered into our Master’s garner. Jesus does not plead for our immediate removal by death. He asks that we may do well in the world, but he never asks for us to be gathered in before we are ripe.
item.content:
“How frequently does the wearied pilgrim put up the prayer, ‘O that I had wings like a dove, for then would I fly away and be at rest.’ But Christ does not pray like that; he leaves it to his Father, until, like shocks of corn fully ripe, we shall each of us be gathered into our Master’s garner. Jesus does not plead for our immediate removal by death. He asks that we may do well in the world, but he never asks for us to be gathered in before we are ripe.” (Sermon on John 17:15)

“The devil is not so concerned with the Christian’s fall into sin, for he knows the blood of Christ can cleanse and restore. What he truly delights in is the Christian’s fall into shame. When a believer is ensnared by shame, he turns his gaze inward, away from the cross, and rather than fleeing to God for mercy, he seeks to make amends by his own efforts, thinking he must do some good thing before he dares to return to the Lord. This is why those who wrestle with lust often regard it as the chief of sins, while the equally grievous sin of pride is overlooked.”

“No heaven will be so sweet as a heaven which has been preceded by torments and pains. Methinks the deeper draughts of woe we drink here below, the sweeter will those draughts of eternal glory which we shall receive from the golden bowl of bliss; the more we are battered … the more glorious will be our victory above.” (Sermon on John 17:15)
